bullets.title: NVDA: Beat/raise but stock uninvestible near-term; trapped in AI doom loop, -25% YTD
bullets.body: NVDA raised FY28 revenue growth guidance to ~75% from ~70% and beat Q3 expectations, but the stock is down ~4% intraday and -25.1% YTD as AI sentiment deteriorates. Buy-side feedback flags NVDA as near-term uninvestible: export controls (BIS approved only 879K of 3.4M requested AI chips for China), fears of Jensen departure, GM compression concerns, and extraordinary early-day dip-buying (+10z in first 30 min) that failed to hold. Goldman notes the GS AI Semis basket trades at just 11x 2028E earnings with consensus expecting 31% growth, but JPM estimates the market is pricing in negative semis EPS growth post-2027.

bullets.title: AMD: -8% on Hunterbrook short report reviving China export-control fears
bullets.body: AMD fell ~8% after Hunterbrook published a short report citing excessive customer commitments relative to cash and China server exposure; AMD disputed the allegations and cited legal compliance. MS notes BIS approved 879K NVDA/AMD AI chips for China Dec 2025–May 2026, far below the 3.4M requested. TSMC and Samsung also halted shipments of advanced chips (16nm and below) to Chinese customers pending Commerce compliance review, widening the export control regime beyond AI accelerators.

bullets.title: AVGO: Google cutting 2027 Broadcom TPU shipments ~20%, shifting to MediaTek
bullets.body: Ming-Chi Kuo reports Google is cutting 2027 Broadcom-designed TPU 8i series shipments by ~1M units (~20%), mostly the higher-priced 8i Max/Whalefish models, and shifting toward MediaTek-designed TPU 8t series. The cut is driven by frontier model development priorities and tight data center power constraints. Mizuho's Dec 8 expert call will cover the broader ASIC competitive landscape including AVGO's position vs. OAI Jalapeno.

bullets.title: INTU: -10% after FY27 guidance cut and $3.68B Mailchimp sale
bullets.body: INTU beat Q1 EPS by 18.3% but cut FY27 revenue guidance and guided Q2 ~14% below consensus, as Credit Karma faces faster-than-expected disruption from AI-powered discovery tools. Mailchimp is being sold to Bending Spoons for $3.68B EV (INTU reinvesting $368M in Bending Spoons equity); divestiture broadly viewed as strategically positive. Street cuts PTs: BMO to $375, KeyBanc to $375, RBC to $330, Stifel at $300 (Hold); NTM P/E compressed to 13x vs. 5-year avg 29x.

bullets.title: DELL: Q3 consensus preview — $49.3B revenue, $6.62 EPS; AI servers the key driver
bullets.body: Consensus expects DELL Q3 ISG revenue of ~$35.3B (+150% y/y), AI-optimized server revenue of ~$19.8B (vs. ~$19B guidance), and FY AI server revenue of $74B (3x y/y). FY non-GAAP EPS consensus is $25.50 (+~150% y/y) on ~$192B revenue (+~70% y/y). DELL stock is +31.2% since Sep 1 vs. S&P +6.3%; options imply ~14.6% post-earnings move. Reports Tuesday post-close.

bullets.title: Semis sector-wide selloff: SNDK, WDC, MRVL, CRDO, COHR, CLS all -4-8% pre-market
bullets.body: Broad semi/hardware selloff in pre-market: SNDK -8.2%, ARM -6.4%, MRVL -5.8%, NVDA -3.9%, AMD -7.1%, WDC -4.5%, STX -4.4%, CRDO -4.0%, COHR -5.1%, CLS -4.5%, GLW -4.2%, CRWV -4.3%, NBIS -4.4%, LITE -5.1%. Export control headwinds, ANT IPO collapse sentiment, and AI capex durability concerns driving the unwind. Six-week hedge fund selling streak in semis is the longest on record; retail liquidated Tech ETFs at the largest-ever weekly rate (-2.0z) with SOXX hitting -11.5z Thursday.

bullets.title: GS semi analyst Schneider: Buy NVDA, AMD, AVGO, CRDO; Sell TXN, ARM
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs semiconductor analyst Jim Schneider is marketing in New York Dec 3-4. Ratings: Buy on ACN, AMD, AVGO, CRDO, NVDA, SNDK, STX; Neutral on INTC, MU, WDC; Sell on TXN, ARM, ENTG, MKSI, SWKS. MRVL is not rated.

bullets.title: CRM: Oppenheimer Outperform, $275 PT; expect Q3 beat but organic reaccel unlikely
bullets.body: Oppenheimer maintains Outperform on CRM (down 30% since September) with a $275 PT into the Dec 2 print. Expects Q3 beat with 100–150bps M&A contribution from Contentful/FIN; F3Q CRPO consensus ~$34.1B (+16% y/y) with 200bps upside. However, Agentforce monetization is more gradual than expected, M&A signals buying growth (viewed negatively), and AI disruption narrative from Anthropic/OpenAI/ServiceNow will persist. Morgan Stanley's headless SaaS framework notes CRM can hold revenue flat with 30% seat loss at 40% price increase.

bullets.title: MSFT, SNOW, PLTR, MDB: Positive readthroughs from Databricks enterprise AI event
bullets.body: Citi flags MSFT, SNOW, PLTR, and MDB as seeing positive demand readthroughs from the Databricks event, which showed accelerating enterprise data/AI consumption but pervasive cost optimization scrutiny. Partners noted higher opportunity for consumption rationalization on Databricks vs. Snowflake. Morgan Stanley's headless SaaS framework favors NOW and TEAM alongside CRM as gated-access players less exposed to AI substitution.

bullets.title: NVDA exploring $500M+ acquisition of Inception Labs (Diffusion AI developer)
bullets.body: NVDA is reportedly in talks to acquire Diffusion AI developer Inception Labs for more than $500M, per pre-market tech sector summary. No further deal terms disclosed.

bullets.title: TRI: JPMorgan flags AI-native legal platforms (Legora) as rising competitive threat
bullets.body: JPMorgan views AI workflow disruption as a more immediate threat to Thomson Reuters than research library displacement. Legora scaled from $1M to $200M ARR in under 24 months across 140,000 lawyers, but JPM notes replicating Westlaw/LexisNexis breadth, trust, and citation infrastructure remains harder than AI workflow competition. Legora does not expect meaningful displacement of Westlaw/LexisNexis in 2027; core competition is other AI-native legal platforms.

bullets.title: TLN: OPCO raises PT to $450 from $400 on 6GW hyperscaler contracting opportunity
bullets.body: Oppenheimer raised its TLN price target to $450 from $400 following management meetings, citing ~6GW of baseload generation available for hyperscaler contracting. Organic opportunities include uprates, batteries, peakers, and powered land; management sees fewer M&A opportunities in PJM. Broader macro context is negative ('quad 4' regime), and OPCO advises selling into any OPEX-driven tactical bounce.

bullets.title: TSEM: Mizuho Outperform, $235 PT; Dec 3 mgmt call on SiPho constraints and margin expansion
bullets.body: Mizuho analyst Vijay Rakesh (Outperform, $235 PT, $15B market cap) is hosting a TSEM management call Dec 3 covering SiPho supply constraint duration, competitive dynamics (GFS and STM ramping), NPO ramp timing (2027), CPO outlook (2029/30), Japan capacity expansion, and margin expansion potential as 300mm adoption accelerates.

bullets.title: ORCL: -3.3% intraday, -52.6% YTD; approaching 52-week lows
bullets.body: ORCL is trading at $106.90, -3.3% intraday and -52.6% YTD, flagged in the 52-week lows screen alongside NVDA (-25.1% YTD), FSLR (-40.9% YTD), IONQ (-53.6% YTD), and BABA (-47.4% YTD). Broad sector weakness concentrated in technology services.

bullets.title: ANET: New R4 platforms for distributed AI inferencing with up to 60% lower power consumption
bullets.body: Arista announced new R4 platforms targeting distributed AI inferencing with up to 60% lower power consumption, per the weekly data center communications note. Broader data center supply is tightening: Loudoun County approved a 12-month DC pause, and Texas resumed permits but new governor-elect Hinojosa plans restrictions post-January 19.

bullets.title: CCL: UBS Buy, $36 PT; new ships add capacity in 2033-35; Celebration Key delayed to 2030
bullets.body: UBS maintains Buy on CCL with a $36 PT. Carnival brand is ordering two ships (3,690 berths each) delivering in 2033 (+90bps capacity) and 2035 (+90bps capacity). The Celebration Key water park opening slips to 2030 (later than expected), with the 2028 expansion adding ~3,000 guests/day capacity. CCL guided for higher yield growth than RCL this year despite no new ship deliveries; Caribbean industry capacity growth slows to +5% in 2027 vs. +12% this year.

bullets.title: WSM: -15% post-earnings; Pottery Barn comps missed, wide Q4 guidance, 25x valuation pressured
bullets.body: WSM beat Q3 EPS by 8.7% but revenue was 0.5% light, with Pottery Barn comps missing by 380bps on reduced promotional activity. Management reiterated FY26 guidance with revenue slightly below consensus; Q4 guidance range is wide. Street cut average PT 4% to $254.10; 44% Buy / 48% Hold / 7% Sell. Elevated fuel/freight costs and ME shipping headwinds flagged for 2027; analysts debate whether Pottery Barn needs reacceleration before shares can rerate.

bullets.title: META: Re-evaluating 2030 net-zero target after 45% GHG surge; halted Class-C offering leaves $60B+ funding gap
bullets.body: META is re-evaluating its 2030 net-zero commitment following a 45% surge in GHG emissions from rapid AI infrastructure buildout. Separately, Citi notes META's halted Class-C share offering leaves a $60B+ hole in funding plans, with trial potentially not starting until April. META plans a $300 Muse Charm device with VZ 5G subsidy targeting 10M units in 2H26.

bullets.title: GOOGL: AI sidebar pushing ads lower; Canadian bond raise for AI buildout
bullets.body: MS notes GOOGL is rolling out an AI sidebar on Search that pushes ads lower, with advertisers already cutting spend (one example: a trophy seller cut monthly spend from $2K to $500). GOOGL also raised C$6B in Canadian bonds to support AI buildout. SemiAnalysis apologized to GOOGL for a prior bearish Gemini call after bullish Gemini 4 performance.

bullets.title: ADI, DELL, HPE, WDAY, ADSK earnings due next week (holiday-truncated)
bullets.body: Key earnings in the Nov 23-27 holiday-shortened week: HPE, ZM Monday post-close; ADI Tuesday pre-open (consensus $4.32B revenue, $3.89 EPS, ~8.4% implied move); ADSK, DELL, WDAY Tuesday post-close (DELL options imply ~14.6% move); DE Wednesday pre-open. Core PCE for October prints Wednesday; markets close at 1pm ET Friday.
